misconceptions.description: Treating hierarchy as visual complexity rather than functional organization
misconceptions.trigger: learner describes hierarchical materials only as 'complex looking'
misconceptions.feedback: Hierarchy matters because each scale contributes a function such as crack control, stiffness distribution, or energy dissipation. It is not just a decorative pattern.

misconceptions.description: Assuming one very strong layer is always better than a layered system
misconceptions.trigger: learner ignores interface design and focuses only on peak material strength
misconceptions.feedback: Many biomimetic systems gain toughness from interfaces and controlled failure paths, not from maximizing the strength of one uniform phase.

misconceptions.trigger: learner explains nacre only in terms of hardness
misconceptions.feedback: Nacre is important because it resists crack propagation through layered architecture and interface mechanics. Toughness is about resisting fracture, not just resisting indentation.
